verdict.rationale: Keycloak's Server Administration Guide documents a first-party Organizations feature: you can create and manage organizations within a realm. Separately, realms act as isolated tenants, and one community user reports running Keycloak in production as a multi-tenant SSO solution. Missing for 10: documented organization membership management, invitation flows, and hands-on corroboration of B2B organization modeling.

support.subject: As a developer, I can model multi-tenant B2B apps with organizations, memberships, and invitation flows out of the box

citations.quote: In the Organizations section, you can manage all the organizations in your realm.
A realm in Keycloak is equivalent to a tenant. Each realm allows an administrator to create isolated groups of applications and users.
We've been using Keycloak in production as a multi-tenant SSO solution for our service delivery.
